top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level FPGA wrapper that provides firmware-visible control/status registers, request packaging, response validation, timeout supervision, safe fallback arbitration, and final bounded actuator command generation. It is the only top-level design entry point and must expose the model transport, cfg_bus, status bits, and actuator command outputs with real RTL drivers. It may instantiate internal control, transport, monitor, and safety-guard submodules, but it does not implement the surrogate model itself.
top_module.functionality: Implements the complete deterministic control wrapper around an external active-aerodynamics surrogate. The top module accepts firmware access through a compact 64-bit control/status window, decodes and stores configuration such as enable, mode select, stream_velocity_setpoint, min/max actuator clamp values, request_timeout_cycles, stale_threshold_cycles, sequence_id, geometry_ref_id, fault_ack, default fallback actuator position, and status bits. It constructs bounded model-request metadata on the request streaming interface, receives bounded model-response metadata on the response streaming interface, validates sequence matching and envelope legality, detects malformed, stale, or late responses, manages timeout counters and inflight state, asserts sticky faults, and arbitrates final actuator output through a dedicated safety-guard stage. Actuator commands are always driven by the safety_guard stage only and are clamped to configured bounds, with a conservative fallback position overriding surrogate-guided output during fault conditions until fault_ack is observed after the fault clears. The module supports architecture-definition mode and cpu_reference deployment path semantics by exposing metadata sufficient for external software/GPU execution while keeping RTL deterministic and synthesizable.
responsibilities: Provide a 64-bit register-memory control/status window for firmware access.
Emit model-request valid/data and accept model-request ready per the mandatory transport direction contract.
Accept model-response valid/data and emit model-response ready per the mandatory transport direction contract.
Package request metadata only, including request_id, sequence, geometry source identifier, geometry format tag, flow condition summary, velocity setpoint, and control flags.
Validate response metadata only, including response_id, sequence, status, health, digest, and compact control recommendation summary.
Generate monotonically increasing sequence numbers and match responses to the outstanding request sequence.
Detect timeout, stale, malformed, and mismatched responses deterministically and set sticky status bits.
Drive safe fallback actuator command on timeout, stale, comm fault, or fault-latched conditions.
Clamp all outgoing actuator commands to configured min/max bounds and assert clamp_active when saturation occurs.
Expose status bits for timeout_fault, stale_fault, comm_fault, clamp_active, fallback_active, request_inflight, and last_sequence.
Keep all datapaths narrow, registered, and FPGA-friendly with no tensor math or large arrays.
Use the memory macro only for any technology-neutral bulk state/history needs and not as a register flattening substitute.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset_n deassertion, clear the inflight request state, deassert request and actuator valid signals, force model_rsp_ready low until the wrapper is initialized, clear transient counters, initialize sequence tracking, and drive fallback-safe actuator behavior. Sticky status bits are cleared on reset and thereafter may only be cleared by explicit fault_ack behavior after the corresponding fault condition has cleared, as defined by the control register contract.
behavior_rules: A request shall be considered valid only when enable is set, the selected mode permits external surrogate operation, the current state machine is not in fault latch, and the request metadata is within the allowed operating envelope.
Sequence numbers shall monotonically increment on each accepted request launch and the response sequence shall be checked against the outstanding request sequence.
If model_req_valid is asserted while model_req_ready is low, the request metadata and valid state shall be held stable until accepted or until a controller-defined abort/fault transition occurs.
Late or malformed responses shall be deterministically dropped and flagged comm_fault and/or stale_fault as appropriate.
Timeout counting shall begin when a request is launched and shall force safe fallback if no matching response is received before request_timeout_cycles expires.
Stale-data logic shall compare current sequence and age against stale_threshold_cycles and assert stale_fault if the age exceeds threshold or if a response arrives after timeout.

Fallback shall drive a conservative default actuator position defined in configuration registers and override any surrogate-guided command until fault_ack is observed after the fault condition clears.
The safety_guard stage shall be the sole producer of actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data.
The actuator command output shall be bounded to configured clamp values, with clamp_active asserted whenever saturation occurs.
The response ready signal shall provide backpressure handling and remain deasserted when the wrapper is not prepared to accept model-response metadata.
All request and response payloads shall remain metadata-only and shall not infer bulk payload RAM in registers.
Any bulk payload/history/FIFO storage required by a downstream implementation shall be mapped through the declared memory macro rather than flattened into registers.
Do not implement surrogate inference, tensor math, ML layers, or geometry tables in RTL.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_cfg_window
modules.description: Register-bank and control/status window submodule that decodes the compact 64-bit cfg_bus transactions into explicit semantic control signals and captures sticky status from the monitor and safety stages. It serves firmware access for enable, mode select, stream_velocity_setpoint, min/max clamps, request_timeout_cycles, stale_threshold_cycles, sequence_id, geometry_ref_id, fault_ack, fallback default actuator position, and status clear/visibility.
modules.functionality: Implements the memory-mapped configuration and status decode/encode layer for firmware. Writes update control registers and read transactions return the configured control state and sticky fault/status bits. The register window does not transport model payloads; it only holds compact control and status values needed by the request packager, monitor, and safety guard.
responsibilities: Decode cfg_bus accesses into explicit semantic control outputs.
Provide a 64-bit readback image for firmware.
Store configuration fields needed by the request packager and safety guard.
Capture status bits from the monitor and safety logic into readable sticky status fields or reportable status mirrors.
Expose fault_ack as a control pulse or level consistent with register programming semantics.
Keep the register set compact and synthesizable.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset clears writable control registers to conservative defaults, deasserts fault_ack, and returns readback/control outputs to a safe state. Sticky status mirror fields are cleared on reset and are updated only from the monitor and safety logic after reset release.
behavior_rules: All register fields shall be compact and 64-bit-window friendly.
No bulk payload storage shall be implemented in registers.
If a write targets an undefined address, cfg_bus_ready may assert without side effects and readback shall remain deterministic.
Status mirrors must reflect the latest explicit monitor/safety inputs and must not be inferred from hidden combinational paths.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
modules.description: Metadata-only request packaging submodule that creates the bounded model request for the external surrogate. It formats request_id, sequence, geometry source identifier, geometry format tag, flow condition summary, velocity setpoint, and control flags into a single 128-bit request payload and asserts valid according to enable, mode, and envelope constraints.
modules.functionality: Packs the semantic request metadata into a bounded 128-bit stream and governs valid assertion based on configuration enable, current mode, envelope legality, inflight state, and fault-latch state. It does not implement the surrogate itself and does not contain large arrays or tensor operations.
responsibilities: Emit model-request valid/data as outputs.
Hold request metadata stable under backpressure until accepted.
Increment and publish sequence information for matching by the monitor.
Prevent request emission when the wrapper is disabled or fault-latched.
Encode metadata only, not bulk payloads.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset deasserts request_valid, clears held request_data, and returns sequence tracking to the configured base state. No request may be emitted while reset is asserted.
behavior_rules: Request metadata shall be valid only when enable and mode conditions are satisfied and the wrapper is not in fault latch.
Request valid and data shall remain stable while model_req_ready is low.
Sequence numbers shall monotonically increment on accepted launches and be driven into the request payload.
No payload wider than 128 bits shall be emitted.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_response_monitor
modules.description: Streaming response validation and timeout supervision submodule. It receives the external surrogate response metadata, checks response_id and sequence matching, tracks age since request launch, rejects malformed or late responses, determines timeout and stale conditions, and provides compact control recommendation and health summary outputs for the safety path.
modules.functionality: Consumes the bounded response stream from the external model and validates it against the outstanding request context. It decodes metadata-only response fields including response_id, sequence, status, health, digest, and recommendation summary. It asserts ready according to internal capacity, accepts only matching and timely responses, discards mismatched or late responses, and raises timeout, stale, or communication faults as needed. It also outputs compact recommendation data that can be used by the safety guard if valid.
responsibilities: Accept model-response valid/data as inputs.
Emit model-response ready as an output.
Validate response sequence against the outstanding request.
Detect late, malformed, stale, and mismatched responses.
Generate compact recommendation and health summary for the safety path.
Provide deterministic drop/reject behavior for invalid responses.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset deasserts ready/accept outputs, clears fault outputs, and clears stored response summaries. No response may be accepted during reset.
behavior_rules: A response is accepted only when it matches the outstanding sequence and the request is still inflight.
Responses arriving after timeout shall be flagged stale and rejected deterministically.
The ready output shall reflect the monitor's ability to accept metadata and shall support backpressure handling.
The recommendation output is compact summary metadata only and shall not contain bulk data or tensors.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_safety_guard
modules.description: Safety arbitration and actuator command stage. It selects between valid surrogate-guided recommendations and conservative fallback position, clamps the command to configured bounds, asserts clamp_active on saturation, and exposes the final bounded actuator command as the only producer of actuator outputs.
modules.functionality: Consumes validated recommendation metadata and produces the final bounded actuator command. If any fault is active or if fallback is latched, the module drives a conservative default actuator position from configuration. Otherwise it uses the recommendation summary as the source command, clamps it to the configured bounds, and asserts clamp_active when saturation occurs. This is the sole legal producer of actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data.
responsibilities: Drive the final actuator command output only from the safety_guard stage.
Override surrogate-guided output with fallback when faults are active or latched.
Clamp the final command to configured min/max values.
Assert clamp_active when saturation occurs.
Assert fallback_active when safe fallback is in effect.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset forces a conservative fallback actuator output, deasserts actuator_cmd_valid, clears clamp and fallback status outputs, and prevents any surrogate-guided command from propagating until reset is released and the control path is initialized.
behavior_rules: The actuator command shall be bounded by the configured min/max clamp values.
The fallback command shall override any surrogate-guided recommendation when a fault is active or latched.
The module shall not generate actuator output from any source other than the safety guard stage.
Clamp status and fallback status shall be explicit outputs and shall be registered.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_status_aggregator
modules.description: Status aggregation and sticky-fault consolidation submodule that merges timeout, stale, communication, clamp, fallback, inflight, and sequence reporting into the externally visible status register signals and top-level status outputs.
modules.functionality: Consolidates status and sticky fault indicators for top-level export and firmware visibility. It captures monitor and safety outputs, holds sticky fault bits until explicit fault_ack behavior clears them after the fault condition has cleared, and forwards the most recent matched sequence number.
responsibilities: Provide the final status register image and top-level status outputs.
Latch sticky timeout, stale, and communication faults until acknowledged under the defined clear condition.
Track clamp and fallback activity status.
Publish inflight and last sequence status.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset clears all sticky status outputs and sequence tracking to safe defaults. Status outputs remain deterministic and low until the monitor and safety stages provide updated inputs after reset release.
behavior_rules: Sticky faults shall only clear after fault_ack and after the corresponding fault source is no longer asserted.
The last sequence status shall reflect the latest completed or tracked request sequence as provided by the monitor.
No implicit or hidden status derivation is allowed beyond the explicit input signals.
